messages:
Amy: quick sync — we need to nail launch criteria + final scope for the Tool/Function Calling API. Sales pushed customers + we have infra constraints. can we list must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
Liam: +1. proposing MVP =: 1) call schema (name, inputs schema) 2) tool invocation message format 3) tool results message with typed output 4) basic auth header flow 5) docs + 2 SDK examples. anything missing?
Jess: from CS: customers care about deterministic outputs for reruns and auditability. they want request/response logging + versioning of tool schemas.
Sara: devex: we need end-to-end examples for node/python, and at least one sample for async callback flows. also playground support for tool mocking.
Omar: security: must-haves are input validation, consent model for running risky tools, and KMS-compatible auth for private deployments. also a threat model doc.
Kai: infra note — streaming tool results is heavier. MVP should support sync and a lightweight async/ callback mode. full streaming (per-token) could be a follow-up.
Amy: summarizing must-haves: schema, call format, results, logging/versioning, auth, docs + SDK snippets, 2 pilot customers. Nice-to-have: streaming, advanced schema types, UI in console. agree?
Liam: we should also decide the schema representation. two options: JSON Schema-ish (compact, widely-known) vs custom typed YAML. I'd vote JSON Schema draft-07 subset to keep validation libs working.
Omar: JSON Schema is fine but restrict features (no remote $ref) to avoid external fetches. require explicit version field in schema metadata.
Jess: customers specifically asked for typed arrays and enums. make sure common types included: string, number, boolean, object, array, enum, oneOf.
Sara: devex: propose an examples folder layout in docs, and sandbox UI that builds a mock tool from the schema. that helps adoption.
Liam: on message format: suggest tool_call message be: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"<name>","inputs":{...},"schema_version":"v1"} and tool_result: {"type":"tool_result","tool":"<name>","status":"ok|error","output":{...},"run_id":"uuid"}. keep minimal fields.
Amy: can you paste small sample for the thread?
Liam: sure:
```
// client -> model
{"type":"tool_call","tool":"get_flight_status","inputs":{"pnr":"ABC123"},"schema_version":"1.0"}
// model -> tool (runtime forwards)
POST /tools/get_flight_status
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
{"pnr":"ABC123"}
// tool -> runtime -> model
{"type":"tool_result","tool":"get_flight_status","status":"ok","output":{"status":"delayed","eta":"2026-03-24T18:30:00Z"},"run_id":"b2f3-..."}
```
Sara: that looks clear. note: include an error structure for validation failures: {code, message, path}.
Kai: latency targets: for Hosted API MVP we should aim <200ms p50 for local tool invocations and <500ms p95 for networked HTTP tools. if customer tools are remote, add SLO slack.
Amy: launch criteria proposal: 1) API spec + JSON Schema subset documented 2) SDKs (py/js) with examples 3) Console: tool registration + mocker 4) Security review + threat model 5) 2 paid pilot customers validated 6) telemetry: latency, error rate, volume, and schema mismatches. any objections?
Omar: need to add audit logs retention policy and opt-in defaults for private deployments.
Jess: add a customer-facing guide on migrating from function-call experiments (since many customers already use ad-hoc patterns).
Liam: implementation plan: phase 1 (4 wks): spec + basic runtime plumbing + sync calls. phase 2 (3 wks): SDKs, console mocker, pilots. phase 3 (open): streaming, advanced schema features, rollouts.
Amy: constraints: Eng capacity limited next 3 weeks (dedicated infra work). propose we start spec + docs now (PM+DevEx) and schedule eng to pick up phase1 in two weeks.
Liam: agree. I'll do a spike this week to validate forwarding model and tracing (KV cache concerns).
Sara: I'll prototype the mocker and playground UI with a minimal schema parser.
Omar: I'll draft security checklist and outline allowed tool permissions + consent UI copy.
Jess: I'll line up 2 pilot customers: FinOps and Marketplace teams showed interest. will confirm commitments by EOD Friday.
Amy: risks: customer asks for streaming + large binary outputs — call out as out-of-scope for MVP. also compatibility for Redwood Private (on-prem) — need simple install/integration docs.
Kai: devops: note that async callback model needs webhook scaling + verification tokens. budget that.
Amy: action items: @Liam spike (owner) due in 5d, @Sara mocker MVP due in 7d, @Omar sec checklist 7d, @Jess customers confirm 3d, docs draft (PM+DevEx) 4d. I'll assemble launch criteria doc and circulate.
deploy-bot: reminder — RFC template for "api/tool-calling" assigned to Amy created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/458
Amy: thanks all. we'll review in sync Wednesday. :thumbsup:
